call_sites: reckon/crew/recovery.py:1197 dispatch_review_for_run composes through _review_dispatch_fields (recovery.py:434) and filters lanes through _failed_review_backend (recovery.py:1104); reached from dispatch_awaiting_reviews and recover

and printed as the retypable command by _review_dispatch_argv (recovery.py:474); reckon/crew/obligations.py:118 reads the composed write_paths to recognise a live hand-launched review of the current head.

findings.text: _stored_review still resolves the head through _reviewed_run_head, whose _review_tree falls back to the run's shared repository once its worktree is gone, while this change composes the dispatch and writes the record at the run's own record head — so for a reclaimed worktree the stored review is invisible to the very reader that decides a review exists: measured with the reviewed module, a complete stored record for the run's head H with the worktree reclaimed returns None from _stored_review (its head read is the repo's HEAD) while select_review_for_head(H) finds that same record, and dispatch_review_for_run (recovery.py:1239) returns early only when _stored_review finds one, so it recomposes a review of H on every cadence and the reviewer rewrites the same record, with classify_pointer (recovery.py:4472, reading _stored_review at :4766) and dispatch_repair_for_run (recovery.py:1620, reading it at :1676) consuming the same mismatch.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against d6e2e039. a5d1d554 adds the head gate to _failed_review_backend; 7cc6d355 moves the comparison onto the run's record once the worktree is gone; 6b4584ce routes _review_dispatch_fields through the same resolver (recovery.py:434) and renames it _run_head_for_review, so composition and comparison cannot drift apart, and it re-heads the backend-selection fixture in tests/test_review_lane_follows_its_run.py so its cases still describe a lane that dropped the current head's review. The one defect I found is not in these lines: the reader side at recovery.py:574 still resolves the head through the checkout fallback, so for a reclaimed worktree the review this change now writes at the run's own head is invisible to the code that decides a review exists — demonstrated below under FINDING.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when names a test over dispatch_review_for_run for both directions; tests/test_rereview_keeps_its_lane.py covers earlier-head keeps the lane (:226), current head still demotes (:248), no recorded head does not demote (:318), a reclaimed worktree reads the record (:268) and a reclaimed worktree composes for the recorded head (:296); I re-ran that file myself at the reviewed head with the module resolving from the reviewed tree: 5 passed, EXIT=0. The file the done-when named second, tests/test_reflex_dispatches_one_repair.py, was never run by the node; the resume advice substituted tests/test_review_reflex_selects_a_backend.py (4 passed, EXIT=0), so the named second arm was replaced by a coordinator instruction rather than skipped silently.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is that a recorded review dispatch counts as a dropped lane only for the head it composed for; at the reviewed head reckon/crew/recovery.py:1089-1127 returns the recorded backend only when the recorded head is non-empty and same_revision to _run_head_for_review, and recovery.py:434 composes the dispatch head and its head-keyed write path from that same resolver, so writer and comparison share one rule and the prior review's finding at recovery.py:433 is repaired; measured on this run's own live pointer with its worktree pointed at a reclaimed path, the old _reviewed_run_head names 6c0793c3 (the shared repo tree) while _run_head_for_review and the run's manifest both name 6b4584ce.
item_verdicts.manifest: read at 12:54; it records four gate commands each with EXIT=0, changed_paths matching the diff, the negative-control log whose first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim, the /tmp deletions, and a landing line naming the measure; it names no baseline_suite or after_suite, and this run was not armed (no suite flag in its dispatch, suite_command None on its pointer), so the added-failure annotation derives as unmeasured rather than as a missing measurement.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the node declares reckon/crew/recovery.py, tests/test_rereview_keeps_its_lane.py and the fragment and figure paths under docs/; git show --stat over a5d1d554, 7cc6d355 and 6b4584ce changes only recovery.py and test files, and the two test files outside the original declaration (tests/test_review_reflex_selects_a_backend.py, tests/test_review_lane_follows_its_run.py) are each named by the coordinator's resume-2-advice.txt grant and declared as a scope exception in the manifest; no fragment was written and the run's own artifact clause says this node writes no figure and no evidence prose, so nothing the prompt owes is missing.

justifications.durability: the negative control at negctl-red.log reddens the earlier-head and no-head cases by name under the declared mutation, and the new composition assertion is a real guard (the fixture's repo head differs from the recorded head), but no test covers the reader/writer head agreement the change creates, which is the state the finding names.
justifications.evidence: the gate names the file the done-when names and its result is recorded in the manifest, and my own re-run of tests/test_rereview_keeps_its_lane.py at 6b4584ce gives 5 passed, EXIT=0 with recovery.__file__ under the reviewed tree.
justifications.fit: sharing one resolver across the two callers matches the module's idiom and the rename reads well, but recovery.py now enforces the record-head rule at :434 and :1116 while the reader at :574 still falls back to the checkout, so the file carries one name for three different answers.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the comparison is exactly the node goal and is asserted both ways at tests/test_rereview_keeps_its_lane.py:225 and :245, and composition at recovery.py:434 now resolves through the same helper.
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path is either declared or named by the coordinator's resume-2-advice.txt grant, and the manifest declares the exception rather than taking it silently.
